#image("/imgs/ap-calc-ab-2019-frq-03-prompt-df0969b9-3806-48a4-83cb-d5dd9bc4502b-1_441_676_717_719.jpg", width: 75%)

The continuous function $f$ is defined on $[-6,5]$. The graph consists of two line segments and a quarter-circle centered at $(5,3)$, and $(3, 3-sqrt(5))$ lies on the graph.

(a) Given $integral_-6^5 f(x) dif x = 7$, find $integral_-6^-2 f(x) dif x$.

(b) Evaluate $integral_3^5 (2f'(x)+4) dif x$.

(c) Let $g(x)=integral_-2^x f(t) dif t$. Find the absolute maximum value of $g$ on $[-2,5]$ and justify.

(d) Find $lim_(x -> 1) frac(10^x - 3f'(x), f(x)-arctan(x))$.
question.solution:
(a) From the graph,
$ integral_-2^5 f(x) dif x = 2 + (9 - 9pi/4). $
Therefore
$ integral_-6^-2 f(x) dif x = 7 - (11 - 9pi/4) = 9pi/4 - 4. $

(b)
$ integral_3^5 (2f'(x)+4) dif x = 2(f(5)-f(3)) + 4(5-3) = 2 + 2sqrt(5). $

(c) Because $g'=f$, candidates are the endpoints and zeros of $f$: $-2$, $-1$, $1/2$, and $5$. The corresponding values are $0$, $1/2$, $-1/4$, and $11 - 9pi/4$. The absolute maximum is
$ 11 - 9pi/4. $

(d) From the graph, $f(1)=1$ and $f'(1)=2$. Thus
$ frac(10 - 3(2), 1 - arctan(1)) = frac(4, 1 - pi/4). $
